questiontext.text:
Goal

A pond warden keeps a list of anything that can quack, including mallards and a wind-up toy. Some entries in the list are empty. Empty entries stay silent. The chorus lists one call per quacker present, in list order, and skips the gaps. Do this without registering types or writing adapters.

Read
  • Interface types. Read the first paragraph. What puts a type in an interface's type set? What value does an interface variable have before assignment? In the File example, what appears between the braces? In the Locker declaration, what appears before those braces?
  • The same section, the paragraph beginning "More than one type may implement an interface". Can S1 and S2 have other methods? Where does the example use the word implements?
Coming from Java

The reflex is implements Quacker on the duck, plus a ToyAdapter so the toy counts too. Go has no implements keyword. The tests build a []Quacker straight from a Duck and a Toy.

class Duck implements Quacker { ... }
class ToyAdapter implements Quacker {
    private final Toy toy;
    public String quack() { return toy.squeak(); }
}
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If the interface declaration fails, compare it with the Locker declaration.
  • Find the initial value of an interface variable in the first paragraph. Compare each pond member with that value.

testcode.text: var q Quacker = Duck{} fmt.Println(q.Quack(), Toy{}.Quack())
pond := make([]Quacker, 2) fmt.Println(len(chorus(pond)), chorus(nil)) pond[0], pond[1] = Toy{}, Duck{} fmt.Println(chorus(pond))

questiontext.text:
Goal

A weather station can accept readings from several kinds of instrument. Its display averages their readings, and its log prints each reading beside the instrument's name. The porch dial has no nameplate, and the hall nameplate takes no readings. An empty display averages to 0. The log prints each reading with %v, so a whole-number reading of 998 prints as 998.

Read
  • io.Reader. Count the declared methods and read the first documentation sentence. What does Reader wrap? Which method gives the interface its name?
  • io.ReadWriter. How does ReadWriter include both Read and Write without repeating their signatures?
  • Implementing an interface. Read the two bullet points. When can a value of one interface type be assigned to another interface type?
Coming from Java

The reflex is one fat Instrument interface beside the hardware, so a dial that only samples needs stub methods. In Go each consumer declares only the methods it calls. A Java Strategy needs an interface and a class per policy, and that consumer interface is the whole pattern.

interface Instrument {
    double sample();
    String name();
    Instrument calibrated(double offset);
}
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If a hidden test will not compile, count the methods on the smallest starter type and compare that count with your Sampler.
  • Compare your Instrument body with ReadWriter's, which has two lines and no parentheses.

Goal

An orchestra programme identifies each player by instrument and seat. The quartet's printer must write "viola" wherever a viola seat appears. The box office still counts those seats as plain numbers.

Read
  • fmt.Stringer. Read the interface and documentation. Which method must a type provide? Which formats make fmt call it?
  • fmt, the Printing section of the overview. Find the numbered rules that fmt applies before printing an operand. Which of %v, %s, %q, %d, and %T reach the rule for a String method?
Coming from Java

The reflex is @Override public String toString(), which every Java print path honours. The second reflex is expecting String.format("%d", seat) to throw when handed an object. Go's fmt decides verb by verb whether to call your method.

@Override
public String toString() { return name + " (" + seat + ")"; }
Required: String
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If Println(Viola) still prints 2, compare your method's name, receiver, and signature against the one line inside the Stringer declaration.
  • For the seat N case, decide from the rule list whether formatting the seat with %d inside String would call String again.

testcode.text: fmt.Println(Viola, Cello) fmt.Printf("%v|%s|%q\n", FirstViolin, FirstViolin, FirstViolin)

expected.text: viola cello first violin|first violin|"first violin"

testcode.text: fmt.Printf("%d %v %T\n", Cello, Cello, Cello) fmt.Println(Seat(7), Player{Name: "Bo", Seat: Seat(7)})

questiontext.text:
Goal

A store interface lists the operations that other code can use. An AI produced a five-method Store interface and a StoreImpl, although the only reader calls one method. Every test passes. Name the one-method interface Getter and make render accept it. Keep every store method reachable from the value NewStore returns.

Read
  • io. Read the first two overview sentences. Which package declares the interfaces? Where do their implementations live?
  • The same page, the Index. Open Reader, ReadWriter, and ReadWriteCloser. How many methods does each declare? How does each interface get its name? Does any type use the word Impl?
Coming from Java

The reflex is StoreService beside StoreServiceImpl in one package, with every public method mirrored in the interface. A factory returns the interface, so the interface belongs to the package that implements it. Every consumer then depends on all five methods.

public interface StoreService { String get(String k); void put(String k, String v); ... }
public class StoreServiceImpl implements StoreService { ... }
Banned: StoreImpl, Store
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Read the first two overview sentences. Is render more like package io or package os?
  • Count the methods render calls. Name the interface as Reader is named after Read.

testcode.text: s := NewStore() s.Put("cy", "violin") fmt.Println(s.Keys(), s.Len(), s.Get("cy"))
s := NewStore() s.Put("di", "violin") s.Put("ana", "viola") s.Delete("di") s.Delete("zed") var g Getter = s fmt.Println(render(g, []string{"di", "ana"}), s.Keys(), s.Len())
a := NewStore() b := NewStore() a.Put("ana", "viola") b.Put("ana", "cello") b.Put("bo", "bass") fmt.Println(render(a, nil), render(b, []string{"ana"}), a.Len()+b.Len(), b.Keys())
